channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Presidential Intervention to Resolve Business Dispute in Issyk-Kul
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has ordered assistance for an entrepreneur facing issues with a planned resort in Jeti-Oguz, Issyk-Kul region. The entrepreneur invested 45 million soms but construction was halted due to encroachment on a protected zone of a brick factory.

item.title: Zelensky suggests US proposal to trade Donbas for NATO membership
item.description: President Zelensky stated that the US proposed considering a new option for resolving the conflict, questioning if Ukraine would withdraw troops from Donbas if it joined NATO. He mentioned ongoing discussions with partners regarding security guarantees, including NATO and EU support, military strengthening, and financial aid for Ukraine's recovery. Zelensky emphasized that any such proposal would be subject to public discussion in Ukraine, as he cannot make such a decision alone. He reiterated that Ukraine would never recognize Russian claims to occupied territories.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans Eco-Friendly Town for Nuclear Power Plant Workers
item.description: Uzbekistan is planning to build a new town for nearly 33,000 residents near its first integrated nuclear power plant in the Farish district of Jizzakh region. The town will feature schools, healthcare, sports, cultural facilities, and green spaces. Eco-urbanism principles will guide its design, focusing on energy and water conservation, and creating a sustainable microclimate.

item.title: Tashkent Experiences Natural Gas Pressure Drop; Ministry Promises Restoration
item.description: Tashkent residents faced a drop in natural gas pressure on November 14. Reports of supply issues came from various districts, with the Ministry of Energy stating that measures are being taken to increase pressure in gas pipelines supplying the capital. The ministry promised to restore normal supply to consumers within the next 2-3 hours.

item.title: UN Chief Guterres Urges Protection for Communities Against Climate Change Impacts
item.description: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for protecting communities from floods, droughts, and rising sea levels due to climate change. He emphasized the critical need for adaptation as global temperatures rise and stressed the importance of early warning systems. Guterres also highlighted the necessity of timely and accessible assistance for those affected when adaptation is no longer possible.

item.title: Pakistan Arrests 82 Afghan Nationals Attempting Illegal Border Crossing
item.description: Pakistani security forces apprehended 82 Afghan nationals in Balochistan province for attempting to cross the border illegally. The group, including men, women, and children, lacked valid residency documents and will face legal proceedings. This incident highlights the ongoing trend of illegal migration from Afghanistan due to post-Taliban conditions.

item.title: Tashkent Police Bust Two International Cybercrime Groups, Arrest 72
item.description: Tashkent police have dismantled two international cybercrime operations, arresting 72 individuals. One group, operating from a rented house, laundered money for illegal online casinos and betting. The second group ran a romance scam call center. Authorities seized over $686,000 in cash and crypto assets, along with numerous electronic devices.

item.title: Tokayev Links National Company Arrests to Constitutional Principles and Reforms
item.description: President Tokayev connected the arrests of leaders from 'Samruk-Kazyna' and 'Kazakhstan Temir Zholy' to the constitutional principle of 'Law and Order.' He stressed that the constitution, adopted by referendum, is a sacred document and disrespecting it is equivalent to discriminating against the people.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan and Azerbaijan Agree on International Road Transport Cooperation
item.description: Kyrgyzstan and Azerbaijan will develop international road transport links following the approval of an agreement by the Kyrgyz Cabinet of Ministers. Signed on July 31, 2026, in Cholpon-Ata, the agreement aims to enhance transport connections and international freight. The Foreign Ministry will notify Azerbaijan of the completion of domestic procedures.

item.title: Widespread Gas Supply Shortages Reported in Tashkent
item.description: The city of Tashkent is experiencing significant gas supply issues due to low pressure in the main gas pipelines operated by Uztransgaz. Responsible organizations are taking measures to normalize the gas pressure. Residents experiencing problems are advised to call 104 or 1104 for assistance and information.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Central Bank Proposes Advance Disclosure of Energy Price Hikes
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has proposed announcing energy tariff changes, including gas, electricity, and heating, several years in advance. This aims to help households and businesses plan expenses and reduce uncertainty. The proposal is part of the monetary policy guidelines for 2027-2029, acknowledging that tariff increases are necessary for energy sector modernization.

item.title: Uzbekistan: Case Against Prevention Inspector Dropped, Released from Custody
item.description: A criminal case against a prevention inspector in Tashkent's Yangikhayot district has been dropped, and the inspector released from custody. An administrative case is pending. The incident involved a conflict between bailiffs and police officers during debt collection.

item.title: Tashkent Residents Report Gas Supply Issues; Low Pressure Cited as Cause
item.description: Residents in eight districts of Tashkent have reported disruptions to their gas supply, with some experiencing a complete outage and others low pressure. The municipal dispatcher attributed the problem to low gas pressure from Transgaz, with measures being taken to restore normal supply.

item.title: WHO Representative Urges Early Diabetes Detection on World Diabetes Day
item.description: The WHO representative in Afghanistan stressed the importance of early diabetes detection on World Diabetes Day. Many are diagnosed after complications arise. People aged 40 and above are urged to get blood sugar tested to protect eyesight and kidney health through timely diagnosis and action.

item.title: South Sudan Presidential Election Postponed to February 2027
item.description: South Sudan's presidential and parliamentary elections, originally scheduled for December 22, 2026, have been moved to February 11, 2027. The National Election Commission announced the updated calendar. Candidate nominations begin November 29, with the final list due January 18, 2027.

item.title: Two Cybercrime Groups Uncovered in Tashkent, 72 Arrested
item.description: Two groups suspected of cybercrime have been exposed in Tashkent, with 72 individuals arrested. They are suspected of involvement in illegal online gambling money transfers and internet fraud. Authorities seized $110,000 in cash and identified a cryptocurrency turnover of $576,000.

item.title: Former Head of Natural Resources Department on Trial in North Kazakhstan
item.description: A trial has begun in North Kazakhstan against the former head of the natural resources department, Yerbolat Bekshenov, and six forestry directors. Bekshenov is accused of fraud and inciting bribery, while the directors face charges related to bribery attempts. The case involves alleged salary irregularities and demands for money.

item.title: Taliban completes reconstruction of 110 kV power line in Faryab province
item.description: The Taliban's economic deputy prime minister's office announced the completion of the 110 kV Maymana-Andkhoi power line reconstruction in Faryab province. The 135-kilometer line cost 145 million Afghanis. Officials claim it will positively impact regional electricity needs, industrial activities, and economic development, reducing reliance on imported power and blackouts.

item.title: Zelensky reveals US proposed NATO membership for Ukraine in exchange for Donbas withdrawal
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that the US has for the first time proposed considering Ukraine's NATO membership in exchange for Ukrainian troops withdrawing from Donbas. Zelensky indicated he would discuss such a proposal with Ukrainian society if confirmed by the US and other NATO members, emphasizing Ukraine would not legally recognize occupied territories as part of Russia.

item.title: Kyrgyz President Orders Investigation into Balykchy Housing Dispute
item.description: Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov has ordered the Ministry of Internal Affairs to investigate the issue of 32 families in Balykchy who cannot register their apartments due to property seizures. These families purchased apartments in 2021, but the properties were later seized due to issues with the construction company, preventing ownership registration.

item.title: Two Underground Call Centers Shut Down in Tashkent, 72 Arrested
item.description: Authorities in Tashkent have shut down two underground call centers involved in illegal financial operations and online fraud. Seventy-two individuals were detained, and the crypto asset turnover reached $576,000. The centers were involved in facilitating illegal online gambling and romance scams.

item.title: Uzbekistan Discusses "One Stop" Customs Control with Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Uzbekistan is exploring the implementation of the "One Stop" customs control principle at select border crossings with Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan. This initiative aims to streamline border procedures by either co-locating customs authorities in one building, dividing export/import functions, or mutually recognizing inspection results to avoid redundant checks.

item.title: US Deportation Plans for Afghans Halted Amid Advocacy and Legal Challenges
item.description: Dozens of Afghans facing deportation from the US to Afghanistan have experienced relief as plans to remove them appear to be on hold. A flight scheduled for election day was grounded by a court order. Advocates warn deportations could be a death sentence, with a rescheduled date looming for some detainees.

item.title: Uzbekistan Prioritizes Gas Supply for Residential and Social Facilities This Winter
item.description: Uzbekistan has approved gas distribution plans for the 2026-2027 autumn-winter season, prioritizing residential homes, schools, kindergartens, and hospitals. Supply may be temporarily restricted for other consumers during severe cold spells to ensure uninterrupted service for priority users.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Proposes Announcing Utility Tariff Changes Years in Advance
item.description: The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has proposed announcing the schedule of changes in utility tariffs several years in advance. This proposal is part of the draft main directions of monetary policy for 2027-2029. The document notes that the increase in prices for some fuel types and regulated services exceeded initial expectations.

item.title: Zelensky: Putin Seeks to Redefine European Borders; Warns of Threats to Finland, Sweden, Baltics
item.description: Ukrainian President Zelensky stated that Putin aims to redefine European borders and identified Finland, Sweden, and Baltic states as countries under threat. He also mentioned that Americans proposed the idea of the US giving territory to Russia in exchange for Ukraine's NATO membership.

item.title: Taliban Arrest Panjshir Man Returning from Iran, Accused of Cooperating with Resistance Front
item.description: Sources report that the Taliban arrested a young man named Ahmad Zabur from Panjshir province about a month ago while he was returning from Iran. He is accused of cooperating with the National Resistance Front. His family has no information about his whereabouts or detention location.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General Investigates Personal Data Leaks and Cybersecurity Committee
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office is conducting a comprehensive review of the Cybersecurity Committee's operations. The investigation focuses on the legality of collecting, storing, and transferring citizens' personal data and the adequacy of protection measures. The probe also examines Yandex service failures and the public release of personal data from educational institutions.

item.title: Afghan Girls Face Continued Oppression and Denial of Education Under Taliban Rule
item.description: Over five years after the Taliban's return, Afghan girls remain deprived of education, with schools and universities closed to them. Their dreams of progress through learning are shattered by the regime's restrictions, confining their activities to their homes. The prolonged denial of education significantly impacts their lives, youth, and aspirations.

item.title: Uzbekistan Seizes Nearly 1.8 kg of Drugs Smuggled from Afghanistan
item.description: Uzbek authorities in the Surkhandarya region have intercepted a smuggling attempt involving nearly 1.8 kilograms of narcotics from Afghanistan. Drugs were found hidden in vehicle parts, including an engine piston containing approximately 400 grams of opium. Further investigation led to the arrest of a suspected recipient in Denov district.

item.title: Over 4.2 Million Afghan Nationals Returned in Two Years, IOM Reports
item.description: The International Organization for Migration (IOM) reported that over 4.29 million Afghan nationals returned to Afghanistan from Iran and Pakistan between January 2025 and November 7, 2026. Returns from Iran decreased by 4 percent, while returns from Pakistan increased by 35 percent. The UNHCR warned of freezing winter conditions for Afghan families.

item.title: Man Suspected of Extremism Propaganda Arrested in Almaty After Receiving 60 Million Tenge
item.description: A 44-year-old man suspected of promoting religious extremism and inciting religious hatred has been arrested in Almaty. He allegedly administered closed Telegram groups and conducted online lectures from abroad since 2024, receiving over 60 million tenge from followers.

item.title: Kyrgyz Ambassador to Japan Replaced; New Envoy Appointed
item.description: Urmat Toktogulov has been appointed as the new Ambassador of Kyrgyzstan to Japan, replacing Erkinbek Osoev. Osoev had served as ambassador since January 2023 and previously held the position of Minister of Transport and Communications.

item.title: Uzbekistan Delegation Attends 'World Atomic Days' Forum in Antalya
item.description: A delegation from Uzbekistan participated in the 'World Atomic Days' forum held in Antalya on November 12-13. The event, organized by Rosatom, focused on the development of nuclear energy, energy diversification, and technological advancements. Discussions included nuclear energy's role in energy security, sustainable development, and climate change mitigation.

item.title: Tashkent Identifies Districts with Highest HIV Detection Rates
item.description: In the first nine months of 2026, Tashkent recorded 307 new HIV cases, a decrease of 17 from the previous year. Bektemir district reported the highest detection rate at 17 cases per 100,000 population. The majority of new infections were sexually transmitted. The Tashkent City Council urged the health department to enhance HIV prevention efforts.

item.title: Tashkent Sees Rise in Mental Health Patients, With Children Forming Nearly Half of New Cases
item.description: Tashkent registered nearly 2,700 new mental health patients in the first nine months of 2026, an increase of 269 from the previous year. Notably, children constitute almost half of these new cases, with 1,300 minors diagnosed. The city's health department has been tasked with improving mental health services.

item.title: US Pentagon Blocks License for Ukraine to Produce Patriot Missiles
item.description: The US Pentagon has blocked the issuance of a license for Ukraine to produce Patriot missile components. Despite prior agreement from the Secretary of State and Secretary of Defense, the final approval is stalled at the Under Secretary of Defense level. The move comes amid Ukraine's critical shortage of Patriot interceptor missiles.

item.title: Almaty Airport Completes Renovation of Domestic Flights Terminal
item.description: Almaty Airport has finished a major upgrade of its domestic flights terminal (T1). The renovation included updated check-in and security zones, baggage infrastructure, and waiting areas. Officials stated the upgrade aims to enhance passenger comfort and strengthen Almaty's role as a regional transport hub.

item.title: Uzbekistan and India to Enhance Control Over Quality and Safety of Medicines
item.description: Uzbekistan and India will strengthen control over the quality and safety of medicinal products. During a scientific expedition to India, specialists from Uzbekistan reached significant agreements in pharmaceuticals and standardization. A memorandum of cooperation was signed with Jamia Hamdard University in Delhi.

item.title: 3.5 Hectares of Agricultural Land in Osh Allocated for Housing Construction
item.description: In Osh, 3.5 hectares of irrigated agricultural land have been reclassified for the construction of a multi-story residential complex with social facilities. The decision, signed by the Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, allows for the development of two state-owned plots previously used for farming. This is an exception to the moratorium on transforming irrigated land.
